strategy.method: Differentiate the Pythagorean relation with respect to time
strategy.why_this_method: The wall, ground, and fixed ladder form a right triangle whose changing legs are linked by one equation.
strategy.alternatives: Solving for y first also works, but implicit differentiation keeps the rates visible.

steps.title: Define the changing quantities
steps.explanation: Both legs change with time, while the ladder length remains 5 metres. The Pythagorean relation connects the two rates.
steps.common_mistake: Do not treat x or y as constant when differentiating in time.

steps.title: Find the height at the stated instant
steps.explanation: The positive root is used because y is a physical height. This gives the missing instantaneous value.

steps.title: Differentiate with respect to time
steps.explanation: Each changing variable contributes a chain-rule rate factor. The derivative of the fixed ladder length is zero.
steps.common_mistake: Include dx/dt and dy/dt after differentiating x squared and y squared.

steps.title: Substitute the instant and solve for the vertical rate
steps.explanation: Insert values only after differentiating, then isolate the requested rate. The negative sign means the height is decreasing.
steps.common_mistake: A downward velocity must be reported with its direction or negative sign.

final_answer.plain: The top is falling at three quarters of a metre per second.
final_answer.domain_notes: At this instant the signed vertical rate is -3/4 m/s.

check.method: substituted both rates into the differentiated constraint

hints: Connect the two changing distances with the fixed ladder length.
Differentiate x squared plus y squared equals 25 with respect to time.
When x = 3, the triangle gives y = 4.
